correctness.rationale: The repaired finding preserves the valid equations and limits. For an idempotent the interval image is fixed pointwise, so monotonicity forces a clamp. A map commuting with it must send the interval into itself; a left extension can climb only when the image of the left endpoint is that endpoint, and the reflected statement holds on the right. These conditions are sufficient pointwise. For h interior rises the binomial walk count has k-h+1 initial positions, with both endpoint enhancements only at h=k. This gives the polynomial also for k=0, when it reduces to (1+z)^N. For k>=1 the double enhancement starts in degree >=3; c_0 and c_2 count rank 1 and rank 3, determining k and AB at fixed n, hence both gaps up to reversal. Summing the base and three enhancements gives the rational series; with y=1 the common numerator is (1-zx)^2+2zx(1-zx)+z^2x^2=1. As an alternate CLT check, the product coefficient makes the excess rank H+Bin(L,1/2) conditional on nonnegative I+H+L=N, with weights (I+1)(L+1)2^L. The probability I+H>=K is bounded by the tail of sum (i+1)2^{-i-h}, since the normalizer is at least (N+1)2^N. A coupling with Bin(N,1/2) then changes the excess rank by O_p(1); the difference between centering the resulting rank at n/2 and at N/2 is negligible. This is uniform over ordered commuting pairs, not uniformly chosen clamps.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration does not certify the unbounded theorem. Reconstruction fixes n, excludes constant clamps, and gives only the reversal orbit.

value.rationale: Commuting maps detect the position of a nonconstant clamp through only ranks 1 and 3, even when the known centralizer cardinality collides (e.g. length four). The joint series and factored aggregate describe actual image rank under a natural pair sampling, yielding an exact finite distribution and a CLT not implied by knowing only the count of pairs. Value is in these uses, not marking the old counting criterion alone.
residual_risks: No inference for arbitrary nonidempotent centralizers or for sampling a uniform idempotent first.
